description_good_justification: README opens by naming the problem and the solution in user-facing language: cortex-viz is a cross-platform MCP server for Codex, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, and any stdio MCP host. It turns Cortex memory, knowledge, sessions, host-neutral live activity, and codebase graphs into six live views; Trace can run without the Cortex database. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/README.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the process explicitly: every change lands through a pull request, there is no direct push to main, issue first for anything larger than a typo, both CI jobs (pytest and vitest) are required, the maintainer reviews and merges, first response within 14 days. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, section 'Requirements for an acceptable contribution': the coding style per language with the selected tool, the structural limits (500-line file, 50-line function, 4 parameters, 3 nesting levels), the mandatory-tests rule, and the copy rule. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
license_location_justification: LICENSE at the repository root: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/LICENSE. pyproject.toml also declares license = "MIT".
documentation_basics_justification: README documents what the software is, how to install it (marketplace, pip, other MCP hosts), the six views, the MCP tools, and the read contract: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/README.md. Architecture: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is twofold and both halves are documented. MCP tool surface (open_visualization, get_methodology_graph) with inputs and outputs: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/README.md#mcp-tools. The HTTP surface the browser consumes, plus the data sources behind it: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
sites_https_justification: Project site and repository are GitHub, HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests: searchable, each message addressable by URL, open to new participants, no proprietary client needed. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/issues
english_justification: All documentation, issues, pull requests, and commit messages are in English.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained. Security, coverage, release, portability, and documentation pull requests were merged through 2026-08-03, including #97. The maintainer and the response commitment are named in https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
repo_track_justification: git, with the full history public since the extraction from Cortex.
repo_interim_justification: Every change is merged to main as its own commit between releases, so main always carries interim work. Published tags through v2.8.0 sit within a longer public commit history.
version_unique_justification: The latest released version is 2.8.0. Each published version is represented by a Git tag and GitHub Release.
version_tags_justification: Every release has a matching vX.Y.Z git tag: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/tags
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md carries a human-written Added/Changed/Fixed summary per version, not a git log dump, with the issue number behind each entry: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md. GitHub Releases mirror it: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: The Unreleased Security section names GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 / CVE-2026-69152, the affected and fixed brace-expansion versions, the development-only scope, and the zero-vulnerability audit result. SECURITY.md also requires public disclosure in the advisory and release notes after a fix ships. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues, linked from the README and CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/issues
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is used for bug tracking and for enhancement requests, publicly and searchably, with every issue in the last six months resolved and closed. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/issues
report_responses_justification: Reports are responded to. Every issue opened in the last six months (#13, #17, #23, #31, #32, #35, #36, #37, #41) received a response and all nine were resolved and closed; none was left unacknowledged.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests get an explicit answer rather than silence. #37 (supply chain) and #35 (JS test harness) were accepted and implemented. The distribution plan evolved explicitly: the Claude plugin remains cortex-viz, while PyPI Trusted Publishing and the MCP Registry use the available canonical identity hypermnesia-mcp-viz.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md: do not open a public issue, open a private GitHub security advisory, with the affected version or commit, reproduction steps, and impact. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private GitHub security advisory, which is a private channel between reporter and maintainer: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/security/advisories/new. Documented in https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last six months, so there is no response time to report against. The commitment is now written down rather than implied: SECURITY.md, 'What happens next', promises initial acknowledgement within 14 days and assessment within 30 days of acknowledgement, with an email escalation path if 14 days pass unanswered. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_justification: PEP 517 build with hatchling, declared in pyproject.toml; `python -m build` produces the wheel and sdist. The release workflow runs exactly that, so the build is automated and reproducible from a clean checkout: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/.github/workflows/Release.yaml
build_common_tools_justification: hatchling and `python -m build`, the standard PEP 517 toolchain. npm plus vitest for the browser test harness.
build_floss_tools_justification: hatchling, build, pytest, vitest, Stryker, ruff, uv, CycloneDX are all FLOSS.
test_justification: Two FLOSS suites, both public and both required in CI: pytest under tests/ (988 passed, 10 skipped on merged main, 2026-08-03) and vitest plus jsdom under tests/js/ (259 passed). How to run them is in CONTRIBUTING.md and in https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_most_justification: Measured on merged main commit 3a11c6653c1aea74c7b57409c6e762bcd6e9993f: required CI runs `coverage run -m pytest`, reports 81% Python statement coverage (11,674 statements, 2,272 missed), and fails below 80%. The run completed 988 tests with 10 skipped; the independent required JavaScript suite completed 259 tests. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/actions/runs/30837051506
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: CI runs both suites on every push and every pull request; the js-test job is required, so a failing JS test fails the build exactly like a failing pytest. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: 'As major new functionality is added, tests for that functionality MUST be added to the automated test suite in the same pull request', and a bug fix requires a regression test that fails on the pre-fix code. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: Evidence from the most recent major changes. #35 added the entire vitest and jsdom harness for the 26k-line browser UI and wired it into CI as a required job. #36 shipped the coverage-honesty feature with its verdict logic as a pure, mutation-gated seam where every emission including the quiet complete state is asserted by tests. #41's file split was behaviour-preserving under the existing suite. See https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
tests_documented_added_justification: The requirement, the command for each suite, and the standard tests are judged by are all in CONTRIBUTING.md, including that strength is measured by mutation rather than line coverage, with the Stryker configuration in stryker.conf.json and surviving mutants triaged in tests/js/MUTATION_NOTES.md. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: CodeQL with the security-and-quality query suite runs on both languages (python and javascript-typescript) on every push, every pull request, and a weekly cron. That suite is a code-quality linter as well as a security scanner: its output on this repository includes unused imports, unused locals, empty except blocks, useless assignments, and trivial conditionals. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
warnings_fixed_justification: Ruff and ESLint are required CI gates, and the CodeQL security-and-quality backlog was triaged and reduced to zero open CodeQL alerts in #97. The merged-main CodeQL workflow passed on 2026-08-03. Scorecard SARIF findings are tracked separately and are not unresolved CodeQL findings. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/actions/runs/30837045047
warnings_strict_justification: Maximally strict where practical, enforced by a required CI job. The `lint` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` over the whole tree on every push and pull request; `js-lint` runs ESLint over ui/. The Python rule set is wider than ruff's default: [tool.ruff.lint].select is E, W, F, I, N, UP, B, C4, SIM, RUF (pyproject.toml). --select ALL is deliberately NOT the target — it reports 6,369 findings here, dominated by docstring-style (D), annotation-completeness (ANN) and assert-in-test (S101) rules that would be answered with a blanket ignore, which is a preference dressed as a gate. Two rules are ignored with the reason written at the ignore: RUF100, because under a curated select it deletes suppressions for rules the set does not enable (it removed 52 of the 60 it flagged, incl. 4 security ones), and SIM105, because ruff's own fixer withholds it at all 42 sites here — every one carries the named failure mode as a comment, which the rewrite would erase. Note on the earlier figure: the 486 violations cited before were measured with ruff's PREVIEW rules enabled, not the defaults; on stable rules the tree passed then and now. The real gate cost was 386 findings under the widened set, all cleared. Closed by https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/issues/45
know_secure_design_justification: Demonstrated in the code and in a written argument rather than asserted. cortex_viz/server/http_security.py implements DNS-rebinding, CORS, header-splitting, and CSRF defenses, each with the CWE it counters named in the docstring (CWE-346/350, CWE-942, CWE-113, CWE-352). The design principles applied (least privilege, economy of mechanism, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, defence in depth, open design) are set out with their concrete instances in https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
know_common_errors_justification: The assurance case enumerates the common weakness classes for this kind of software (injection, path traversal, XSS, CSRF, DNS rebinding, permissive CORS, header injection, hardcoded credentials, supply-chain tampering), states the countermeasure for each, and marks the two that are not yet fully argued rather than claiming them: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
crypto_published_justification: cortex-viz implements no cryptography. It stores no passwords, mints no keys, tokens, or nonces, and runs no cryptographic protocol: it is a local read-mostly visualization server bound to 127.0.0.1. Release signing is delegated entirely to Sigstore via GitHub's attest-build-provenance action, so no signing key is handled by this project's code.

delivery_mitm_justification: Every delivery path is HTTPS or ssh: the Claude Code plugin marketplace over HTTPS, `git clone` over HTTPS or ssh, and GitHub Release assets over HTTPS. No installation step retrieves anything over plain HTTP.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is fetched over HTTP and used. Release assets carry .sha256 companions served over HTTPS, and each artifact additionally carries a Sigstore build-provenance attestation verified with `gh attestation verify <file> --repo cdeust/cortex-viz`, which is a signature check rather than a bare hash comparison. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/.github/workflows/Release.yaml
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known unpatched vulnerability of medium or higher severity remains. On 2026-08-03 GitHub published GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 / CVE-2026-69152 for brace-expansion; the lockfile was immediately updated from affected 5.0.8 to fixed 5.0.9 and `npm audit --package-lock-only` returned zero vulnerabilities. This dependency is confined to the private JavaScript test harness; package.json declares no runtime dependencies and it does not ship in the Python wheel. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: npm audit reports zero vulnerabilities on 2026-08-03 after the earlier test-toolchain remediation and the immediate brace-expansion 5.0.8 to 5.0.9 update for GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895. The required JavaScript suite passes all 259 tests.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential is committed. DATABASE_URL is user-supplied configuration (plugin setting or environment variable), defaulting to a local, credential-free postgresql://127.0.0.1:5432/cortex; the project mints no secrets of its own. CodeQL runs continuously over both languages and OpenSSF Scorecard over the repository, and neither reports a leaked credential.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL with the security-and-quality suite, on BOTH languages, because cortex-viz is half browser-executed code: the standalone server is Python but the UI it serves is 98 JS files and about 26k lines that run in the user's browser. It runs on every push, every pull request, and a weekly cron, so a new query pack landing against unchanged code is still caught. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml. OpenSSF Scorecard additionally grades repository posture weekly: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/.github/workflows/scorecard.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: The security-and-quality suite includes CodeQL's security queries for both languages. It surfaced the historical py/path-injection, js/remote-property-injection, and js/incomplete-html-attribute-sanitization findings that were triaged and closed in #97; zero CodeQL alerts remain open.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The CodeQL security-and-quality backlog was triaged in #97. The real path-containment and incomplete attribute-escaping defects were fixed with regression tests; analyser-model mismatches were rewritten onto the shared containment primitive. Zero CodeQL alerts remain open, and the merged-main CodeQL workflow passed on 2026-08-03. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/pull/97 and https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/actions/runs/30837045047
static_analysis_often_justification: Every push, every pull request, and a weekly Monday cron, so inaction does not hide a new query pack. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is applied. There is no fuzzer against the HTTP request surface and no web application scanner against the served UI, which are the two that would fit this product. The 988 pytest and 259 vitest tests are a functional gate, not dynamic analysis, and the assurance case says so rather than counting them here. This is SUGGESTED, and it is recorded as not done rather than reinterpreted.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: No memory-unsafe language is used. The project is Python and browser JavaScript only; there is no C, C++, or unsafe Rust anywhere in the tree, and no compiled extension is authored by this project.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic analysis is run (see dynamic_analysis), so there is no dynamic-analysis configuration in which to enable assertions. Recorded as Unmet rather than N/A because the honest reason is that the prerequisite is missing, not that the criterion cannot apply.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic code analysis is performed, so no vulnerability has been discovered by that means. This is the disposition the criterion's own details prescribe in that case.
achieve_passing_justification: All passing MUST criteria are Met or N/A in this file, with each SHOULD and SUGGESTED answered from measurement.
dco_justification: No Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off is required and no DCO bot is configured. CONTRIBUTING.md instead states that by opening a pull request a contributor affirms they wrote the contribution or have the right to submit it under the MIT license. On a single-maintainer project with no external contributors to date, a DCO bot would add a gate without adding an assurance anyone is currently relying on. This is a SHOULD and it is recorded as not done. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#sign-your-work
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md states how decisions are made (ordinary changes by maintainer review on the pull request, design and scope changes discussed in a public issue first, security changes privately until a fix ships), and that everything except unfixed vulnerabilities is decided in public. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
code_of_conduct_justification: Contributor Covenant 2.1, adapted, with the enforcement contact (admin@ai-architect.tools) and an explicit note that a single maintainer both receives and decides reports, plus the GitHub escalation path if the report concerns the maintainer. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a table of the three roles (Maintainer, Contributor, Reporter) with the responsibilities and the concrete permission each is held by, and names who holds the maintainer role. It also states that there are currently no committers besides the maintainer. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
access_continuity_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the credential-free continuation path. The complete source, history, tests, plugin manifests, release workflow, and design record are public under MIT. A successor can fork, enable and manage Issues, accept pull requests, and publish an attested tagged release under the fork's own GitHub OIDC identity within a week; no original signing key, registry token, domain, private dependency, or legal assignment is required. Users install from the continuation repository and past releases remain independently verifiable. @cdeust is still the only administrator of the original repository, so the bus factor remains 1 and preserving its URL/listings is weaker than with a second maintainer; that does not prevent continuation of the project results and the three required operational capabilities: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity-stated-honestly
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1. See access_continuity and https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/issues/48. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity-stated-honestly
documentation_roadmap_justification: docs/ROADMAP.md gives the current state, a near-term section whose items are the assurance gaps named in this file (each with its issue number), medium and longer-term direction, and an explicit 'Not planned' section. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md
documentation_architecture_justification: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md documents the two halves (Python server and browser UI) and how they talk, the five Python layers with the inward dependency rule and the file count per layer, the structural invariant that no `import mcp_server.*` is permitted anywhere in cortex_viz/, the read contract per data source, the browser directory map, the four trust boundaries in order of exposure, and the build and release path. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_security_justification: Two documents. SECURITY.md covers what cortex-viz accesses, what it writes, the supply-chain assurance and how to verify it, the reporting process with timelines, reporter credit, and scope: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/SECURITY.md. docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the architectural security documentation: assets, adversaries, per-boundary argument, secure design principles, common weaknesses, and an explicit statement of what the case does not cover: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
documentation_quick_start_justification: README 'Getting Started' is two commands (marketplace add, plugin install) followed by /cortex-visualize, with a no-database path that needs no setup at all: the Trace view runs against ~/.claude session files alone. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/README.md#getting-started
documentation_current_justification: Documentation is corrected when it is found wrong, not left to drift. This change alone corrected a blanket 'read-only / does not write' claim in README, SECURITY.md, and PRIVACY.md that was factually wrong (cortex-viz writes five derived-cache tables of its own, including session_activity) and narrowed a UI-fingerprint claim in SECURITY.md that overstated its coverage of CDN-loaded scripts. CONTRIBUTING.md requires that an observable change updates CHANGELOG.md and an interface change updates the README in the same pull request.
documentation_achievements_justification: README displays the OpenSSF Best Practices badge for project 13846 and records the Silver level earned on 2026-08-03, the OpenSSF Scorecard score of 7.2 on the same date, and the independently verified Sigstore provenance for all four v2.8.0 release artifacts with the exact verification command. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/README.md#achievements
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: No accessibility standard has been applied or tested against. The product is a dense data-visualization surface (SVG, canvas, and WebGL graph views with hover-driven detail), which is the hard case for accessibility, and no keyboard-only navigation audit, screen-reader pass, or WCAG contrast check has been done. Two things point the right way but neither was done for accessibility reasons and neither is evidence: the palette is resolved from design tokens at runtime with a persistent light/dark surface toggle, and every count on screen is exact text rather than a graphic. Recorded as not done rather than claimed from those.
internationalization_justification: No internationalization. All UI strings are hardcoded English literals in the JS files with no message catalogue, no locale detection, and no externalized strings. The data rendered (memories, session transcripts, file paths) is passed through unmodified and so displays in whatever language the user's own content is in, but that is a property of not touching the data, not i18n support. No translation has been requested; this is a SHOULD and it is recorded as not done.
sites_password_security_justification: The project operates no site that accepts passwords. The repository and issue tracker are GitHub, which handles its own authentication, and cortex-viz itself has no accounts, no login, and no password storage of any kind: it is a local server bound to 127.0.0.1 with no authentication subsystem.
maintenance_or_update_justification: There is a single supported line and a documented upgrade path, which is what this criterion asks of a project this size. Upgrading means reinstalling the plugin (or `pip install -e .` from a clone); no configuration migration has ever been required, and no interface removal has occurred across the 2.x series. Breaking changes and their migration steps are recorded per version in https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md. Older versions are not backported: users move to the newest, which is stated rather than implied.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: SECURITY.md, 'Credit': reporters are credited by name in the security advisory and the release notes unless they ask not to be, and are invited to state in the report which name or handle they want used or that they prefer to remain anonymous. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md, 'What happens next', publishes the process and its timelines: acknowledgement within 14 days, assessment of severity and affected versions within 30 days of acknowledgement, fix or a written dated plan tracked in the advisory, public disclosure after the fix ships, with an email escalation path if 14 days pass unanswered. The scope of what is and is not covered is stated in the same file. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/SECURITY.md
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names the style guide per primary language and the tool for each: PEP 8 for Python with the project's [tool.ruff] configuration in pyproject.toml, and for the browser UI vanilla ESM and IIFE with no bundler or framework, matching the file being edited. It also states the structural limits that review enforces (500-line file, 50-line function, 4 parameters, 3 nesting levels), which are the standard behind issues #17, #23, and #41. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Both languages are automatically enforced by required CI jobs. Python: `lint` runs `ruff check` (rule set in [tool.ruff.lint].select) plus `ruff format --check`; ruff is pinned in the dev extra (>=0.15.0,<0.16.0) and installed from uv.lock, so CI runs the same version a contributor does. JavaScript: `js-lint` runs `npm run lint` (ESLint 10 flat config, eslint.config.mjs) over ui/, with a rule set scoped to what a reader cannot catch in one file — no-undef, no-implicit-globals, no-redeclare, no-unused-vars and the always-a-bug rules — since the UI is vanilla script-tag JavaScript with hand-maintained load order and no bundler. Vendored minified bundles under ui/**/vendor/ are excluded. Wiring it found and fixed three variables (domainsSeen, globalCount, hotCount in ui/unified/js/knowledge.js) that were assigned without declaration and so leaked onto window. Closed by https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/issues/45
build_standard_variables_justification: There is no make or configure build to pass variables to. The build is PEP 517 via hatchling, driven by pyproject.toml, where the equivalent settings are declarative rather than variable-driven, and the browser UI ships as static assets with no build step at all.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Nothing is compiled, so there is no debug-information or symbol-stripping step to preserve. Python source ships as source in the wheel and the UI ships unminified and unbundled, which means the shipped JavaScript is already the readable original.
build_non_recursive_justification: There is no recursive make. The build is a single PEP 517 hatchling invocation.
build_repeatable_justification: This is the disposition the criterion prescribes for scripting languages where the source is used directly rather than compiled. Python source and the static UI tree are shipped and executed as-is. The integrity property this criterion protects is provided by different means here and is verifiable: a sha256sum manifest over the whole ui/ tree, per-asset checksums, and a Sigstore build-provenance attestation binding every artifact digest to this repository, workflow, and commit.
installation_common_justification: The standard mechanism for the primary Claude Code interface is the plugin marketplace (`claude plugin marketplace add cdeust/Cortex` then `claude plugin install cortex-viz`). Starting with the v2.8.0 release, other MCP hosts can install the standard PEP 517 distribution with `pip install hypermnesia-mcp-viz`; it exposes both hypermnesia-mcp-viz and the compatible cortex-viz stdio commands. Before that release, the documented non-plugin path is an editable install from the repository. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/README.md#install
installation_standard_variables_justific: There is no bespoke installer with prefix or destination variables. Installation is delegated to pip and to the plugin host, both of which honour their own standard location and environment conventions.
installation_development_quick_justifica: `git clone`, `pip install -e ".[dev]"`, `python -m pytest` gets a working development environment, and `npm ci && npm test` the browser half. Critically, no external infrastructure is needed to run it: `CORTEX_VIZ_NO_DB=1 python3 -m cortex_viz` starts the server with no Cortex install and no PostgreSQL, serving the Trace view from ~/.claude session files alone. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#running-the-suites
external_dependencies_justification: Computer-processable and complete on both halves. Python: pyproject.toml declares runtime dependencies and the viz-tile, community, data, and dev extras, with uv.lock pinning the resolved graph; every release additionally ships a CycloneDX SBOM (cortex-viz.cdx.json) generated from that lock. JavaScript: package.json plus package-lock.json, devDependencies only, since the harness ships nothing. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/pyproject.toml
dependency_monitoring_justification: Two independent mechanisms. Dependabot covers all three dependency surfaces weekly (pip, npm, and github-actions, the last so SHA-pinned actions still receive security updates): https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml. OpenSSF Scorecard grades dependency posture weekly: https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/.github/workflows/scorecard.yml. Stated honestly, this is new: nothing was watching before, which is exactly why 19 npm advisories in the test harness had gone unnoticed until a manual audit on 2026-07-28 (https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/issues/49).
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Reused components are standard registry packages with no forked or vendored convenience copies to diverge: Python via pip and pyproject.toml, JavaScript devDependencies via npm, GitHub Actions SHA-pinned with the version in a trailing comment so Dependabot rewrites pin and comment together. The ui/ tree is first-party source, not a vendored third party. One qualifier, recorded rather than omitted: four UI pages load three.js and 3d-force-graph from the unpkg CDN. Those are version-pinned in the script tag, so identifying and updating them is trivial, but they carry no Subresource Integrity hash and are outside the release fingerprint; https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/issues/50 proposes vendoring them, which would also close that gap.
interfaces_current_justification: The documented interface matches the shipped one. Both MCP tools (open_visualization with its view parameter, get_methodology_graph) are documented in the README as implemented, and the data sources behind the HTTP surface are tabulated in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md against the current code. CONTRIBUTING.md requires an interface change to update the README in the same pull request.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: CI runs on every push and pull request, exercising the assembled system rather than isolated units: 988 pytest tests including HTTP endpoint and server-integration suites, and 259 vitest tests that load the real ui/ sources into jsdom and assert cross-module behaviour. Both jobs are required and report pass or fail per run. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: The practice holds for defects in code that the suites can reach. #35's fix to the DB-skip fixture, which had silently become a no-op because MemoryReader was lazy, shipped with the corrected assertion; #36 landed its verdict logic as a pure seam with every emission asserted, including the quiet complete state, and gated by Stryker rather than by line coverage. Two of the last six months' fixes carry no test and the reason is stated rather than hidden: #31 was user-visible copy (em-dash removal) and #39 was a CI workflow fix whose failure mode was startup_failure on main, verified by workflow_dispatch post-merge because a push-and-schedule-only workflow is invisible to pull-request CI. Neither is testable by the pytest or vitest suites. The rule is now written down rather than customary: CONTRIBUTING.md requires a regression test that fails on the pre-fix code. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Measured on merged main commit 3a11c6653c1aea74c7b57409c6e762bcd6e9993f. Required CI runs `coverage run -m pytest`, emits `coverage report --show-missing`, and enforces `fail_under=80`. The run completed 988 tests with 10 skipped and measured 81% Python statement coverage: 11,674 statements, 2,272 missed. The separate required JavaScript suite completed 259 tests. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/pull/97 and https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/actions/runs/30837051506
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states it as a requirement in the imperative, not as encouragement: 'As major new functionality is added, tests for that functionality MUST be added to the automated test suite in the same pull request', followed by 'a pull request that adds behaviour without tests will be sent back', and separately that a bug fix requires a regression test failing on the pre-fix code. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests-are-mandatory-for-new-functionality
implement_secure_design_justification: The principles are applied concretely and the instances are auditable. Least privilege: Cortex's memory tables are never written and the ban on `import mcp_server.*` keeps the separation structural; workflow tokens are permissions: read-all by default and widened per job only where a job must write. Fail-safe defaults: binds 127.0.0.1 and never 0.0.0.0, an unreachable database degrades to a named no-DB mode rather than erroring or inventing data, and an unknown static path returns 403 or 404 rather than guessing. Complete mediation: Host, Origin, and same-origin checks run per request in the handler path, not once at startup. Defence in depth: three independent controls on the browser-to-server boundary with distinct failure modes, so a cross-site write requires two of them to fail. Economy of mechanism: no bundler, no framework, no plugin system, no authentication subsystem. Set out with the per-boundary argument in https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: cortex-viz implements no cryptography. It stores no passwords, mints no keys, tokens, or nonces, and runs no cryptographic protocol: it is a local read-mostly visualization server bound to 127.0.0.1. Release signing is delegated entirely to Sigstore via GitHub's attest-build-provenance action, so no signing key is handled by this project's code.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The one credential-bearing value cortex-viz handles is DATABASE_URL, which may embed a database password. It is supplied entirely as external configuration, either the plugin's database_url user setting or the DATABASE_URL environment variable, is never written into a configuration file the project ships, never committed, and never logged. Changing or rotating it requires no code change, no rebuild, and no reinstall: set the value and restart the server. The project stores no other credential and no private key of its own.
crypto_used_network_justification: Answered against what the software does rather than reinterpreting the question. The HTTP server speaks plain HTTP, not HTTPS. The mitigating facts are real: it binds 127.0.0.1 only, so traffic never leaves the loopback device and there is no network path for an interceptor to sit on, and requests are gated by a Host-header allowlist, an Origin allowlist, and a same-origin check on writes. TLS on loopback would add certificate generation, trust-store, and rotation burden for a local developer tool without countering a threat in the model (a local process capable of sniffing loopback can already read ~/.claude and the database directly). The one outbound request the product makes, the CDN library fetch, is HTTPS. This is a SHOULD, and it is recorded as not met with the reasoning, rather than marked N/A on the grounds that loopback is not a network. See https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md sections 3.1 and 3.5.
crypto_tls12_justification: The project implements no TLS and terminates no TLS connection: the server is plain HTTP on loopback. The one HTTPS request in the product is the browser's own fetch of a CDN library, where protocol version selection belongs to the browser and to unpkg, not to this software.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The software does not use TLS itself, so there is no certificate for it to verify. The CDN subresource fetch is performed by the browser, which verifies the certificate under its own policy.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The software does not use TLS, and sends no private information over one. It has no cookies, no sessions, no tokens, and no authentication headers of any kind.
signed_releases_justification: Release v2.8.0 publishes a wheel, sdist, CycloneDX SBOM, and UI fingerprint manifest plus SHA-256 companions. On 2026-08-03 every checksum was recomputed successfully and every primary artifact passed `gh attestation verify <file> --repo cdeust/cortex-viz`, binding its digest to this repository's SHA-pinned Release workflow through GitHub OIDC and Sigstore's transparency log. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/releases/tag/v2.8.0
version_tags_signed_justification: Version tags are lightweight Git tags and are not independently signed, so this suggested criterion remains Unmet. Release v2.8.0 artifacts themselves are covered by verified Sigstore provenance, recorded separately under signed_releases.
input_validation_justification: Untrusted input is checked against allowlists and rejected, not sanitized-and-hoped. cortex_viz/server/http_security.py allowlists loopback Host and Origin values, rejects response-header control characters, and enforces same-origin writes. Every request-derived filesystem path now passes through the shared symlink-aware containment primitive before use. The full CodeQL path-injection triage and regression suite landed in #97; zero CodeQL alerts remain open. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/pull/97
hardening_justification: No hardening mechanism is applied in the sense this suggested criterion means. The server sends no Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or frame-ancestors restriction. The historical DOM-escaping findings were fixed and CodeQL is clear, but a CSP would still limit damage from any future rendering defect and constrain the CDN loads tracked in https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/issues/50. Existing loopback, Host, Origin, and CSRF controls are access controls, not hardening, so this answer remains Unmet.
assurance_case_justification: docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md contains all four required elements. Threat model: six numbered adversaries and STRIDE categories. Trust boundaries: four, identified and ordered by exposure. Secure design principles: seven principles tied to concrete controls. Common implementation weaknesses: twelve classes with current status. The formerly incomplete request-path and DOM-rendering arguments were closed through #97 and zero open CodeQL alerts; the document still states the first-party scope limit around CDN-loaded libraries. https://github.com/cdeust/cortex-viz/blob/main/docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
_comment: OpenSSF Best Practices evidence for project 13846. Silver was earned on 2026-08-03 after documenting fork-based access continuity, exceeding 80% statement coverage on merged main, and independently verifying every v2.8.0 artifact's Sigstore provenance. The bus factor remains 1; Gold's second-maintainer and two-person-review requirements still depend on #48. See docs/ROADMAP.md.
